title: digits
summary: Get or set the default variable-precision digit count.

gpu_support.notes: The precision setting is host runtime state for symbolic variable-precision formatting.

description: `digits` returns the current default precision for `vpa`. `digits(d)` rounds a finite numeric scalar to the nearest integer, sets that precision, and returns the previous value as a double scalar. RunMat mode additionally supports `digits('default')` as an explicitly gated reset extension.
behaviors: The default value is 32 significant digits.
The public precision range is 2 through 100000000 significant digits, inclusive, and noninteger floating controls round to the nearest integer.
Host controls can use single, double, or any of the eight built-in integer classes; logical and resident controls reject.
Numeric text and the `'default'` reset are named RunMat-only extensions and reject in MATLAB-compatible mode.
The setting affects later `vpa(x)` calls that omit an explicit precision.

faqs.question: Does `digits` change ordinary double precision arithmetic?
faqs.answer: No. It only controls the default significant-digit count used by symbolic variable-precision operations such as `vpa`.
